How to Qualify for Low-Income Housing
How to Qualify for Low-Income Housing
Documents you'll need to qualify and resources you can use to find an affordable apartment
Julie Aiello
-
Last Updated: February 2, 2022
iStock.com/ RomanBabakin
Low-income housing provides housing opportunities for people who are unable to afford ever-rising rental rates. There are two main types of low-income housing:
Public Housing: Housing units managed by the local housing authority that offers affordable rentals to low-income households. The units are priced based on a percentage of one’s income.
Section 8: A program that provides subsidies or vouchers to make up the difference between an area’s rental rates and what low-income families can actually afford. These vouchers can be used in any housing unit where Section 8 is accepted.
How to qualify for low-income housing
You might be wondering, “How do I qualify for low-income housing?” To start, you’ll need to know your county’s definition of “low-income”. For example, a family of four living in San Francisco with a combined yearly income of $129,000, or less, would qualify for low-income housing. In New York City, that number is $85,350. Meanwhile, in Chicago, it’s $71,300. These limits change yearly, so check out this Housing & Urban Development (HUD) calculator to find out the most up to date income limits for your county.
The best way to find out if you qualify for low-income housing (both Public Housing and Section 8) is to contact your local housing authority. To find the contact information for Public Housing Agencies in your city, visit the HUD website. Most local housing authorities maintain their own websites, too, so you can find relevant information by searching for your local housing authority online.
After you determine that you qualify for low-income housing, you will need to verify your income with the HUD. To show proof of income, you can use:
Recent pay stubs
Invoices
IRS tax returns
You may also be required to provide a rental history, pass a criminal background check, and provide proof that you are a U.S. citizen or legal resident.
Finding an apartment
Once you’ve confirmed that you are eligible for low-income housing, the next step is to find an apartment. A great place to start is on Zumper, filtering by income restriction, price, or Section 8-friendly apartments. You can also look through the Affordable Housing Search on HUD’s website. A great comprehensive resource can be found on this affordable housing guide.
Once you’ve found a few affordable options, obtain and complete the rental application. You’ll want to have household information readily available. For all residents who will be living in your housing unit, you will need their:
Full names
Income amount and proof of income
List of individuals’ assets
Social security numbers
Information on how to submit each application varies, but each living community or landlord will provide it prior to giving you the application. Be sure to follow each community’s instructions and submit the applications accordingly. You may be put on a waiting list and, if you are, you may be contacted and asked if you want to remain on the waitlist. Respond immediately to avoid being terminated from the list.
What if my income changes?
It’s important to be honest about any changes to your income. If you’re caught hiding information or lying about your income, you could risk losing eligibility completely. If you receive a raise or any other type of additional income, report it to your Public Housing or Section 8 caseworker immediately. The most likely scenario is that you will not have to move, but you may have to pay a slightly higher rent each month going forward.
Other Considerations
Depending on where you live, the time it takes to get approved for a Public Housing or Section 8 unit could be lengthy. Cities nationwide are dealing with massive waiting lists; many cities have even been forced to close their waiting lists with no date set for reopening them. Speak with your local HUD to see what the low-income housing restrictions are in the city where you want to relocate.
Looking for your next apartment? Search thousands of apartments on Zumper and find one that matches your income and preferences.

Qualifying For A Low Income Housing Tax Credit
A low income housing tax credit may be available to low income earners that qualify. Meeting the qualification for the credit requires an individual to understand the requirements for the credit. An individual taxpayer that is a low income earner must file a tax return, regardless of whether the individual owes taxes or not.
What a Low Income Tax Credit Is
A low income tax credit is a reduction in taxes that is applied to an individual tax return. This is done when an individual files a full tax return where they itemize their deductions. For low income earners however this is not possible since low income earners do not itemize their taxes. The credit would be available as an upfront payment that is available based on the individual’s income and tax status.
Rules for Qualifying
The rules for qualifying for a low income housing credit can be found on the IRS.gov website. Many communities also make available information through their department of housing and through community-based organizations. This helps a low income earner to understand the requirements and how to apply for the housing credit.
What is a Low Income Earner?
Most low income earners are considered to be at or below the federal poverty level. This is typically $44,000 for a family of 4 or $11,000 for an individual. Qualifying as a low-income earner is essential in order to receive the low income housing credit. In addition, a low income earner must file a tax return, even if the taxpayer does not owe or have to file a return. The return provides information necessary for the IRS and requisite program to qualify the individual as a recipient of a low income housing tax credit.
The Process for Qualifying
A person who believes that they qualify low income housing tax credit should inquiry through a local housing assistance program about the requirements. This is the first step in gaining information about the program and the level of assistance that is available. Once this is accomplished, a housing program can assist the low income taxpayer in preparing an application or necessary forms to receive the credit. This assistance is generally available in every community and is advertised freely to low income earners.
